lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: What is the use of a book without pictures or conversations?

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice-sister
lines.text: Hush, Alice dear.

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: I wonder how many miles I've fallen by this time?

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: Dinah'll miss me very much to-night, I should think!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: Do cats eat bats? Do cats eat bats?… Do bats eat cats?

lines.speaker: CHAR-white-rabbit
lines.text: Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be late!

lines.speaker: CHAR-white-rabbit
lines.text: Oh my ears and whiskers, how late it's getting!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: That certainly was not here before.

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: No, I'll look first, and see whether it's marked 'poison' or not.

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: What a curious feeling! I must be shutting up like a telescope.

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: For it might end, you know, in my going out altogether, like a candle.

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: Come, there's no use in crying like that! I advise you to leave off this minute!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: Well, I'll eat it. And if it makes me grow larger, I can reach the key;

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: and if it makes me grow smaller, I can creep under the door.

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: So either way I'll get into the garden, and I don't care which happens!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: Which way? Which way?

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: Curiouser and curiouser!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: Now I'm opening out like the largest telescope that ever was! Good-bye, feet!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: You ought to be ashamed of yourself, a great girl like you, to go on crying in this way!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: Stop this moment, I tell you!

lines.speaker: CHAR-white-rabbit
lines.text: Oh! the Duchess, the Duchess! Oh! won't she be savage if I've kept her waiting!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: If you please, sir—

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: Dear, dear! How queer everything is to-day! And yesterday things went on just as usual.

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: I wonder if I've been changed in the night? But if I'm not the same, who in the world am I?

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: Ah, that's the great puzzle!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: Let me see: four times five is twelve, and four times six is thirteen… London is the capital of Paris—

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: No, that's all wrong, I'm certain! I must have been changed for Mabel!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: Oh dear, I do wish they would put their heads down! I am so very tired of being all alone here!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: That was a narrow escape!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: And now for the garden!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: I must have fallen into the sea! And in that case I can go back by railway.

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: I wish I hadn't cried so much!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: I shall be punished for it now, I suppose, by being drowned in my own tears!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: That will be a queer thing, to be sure! However, everything is queer to-day.

lines.speaker: CHAR-jie-rui-er
lines.text: First time on Trantor? I'm Jerril. Just Jerril.

lines.speaker: CHAR-jie-rui-er
lines.text: See the chrome bars? Locals don't even look at them. You will.

lines.speaker: CHAR-jie-rui-er
lines.text: Feet under the bar — there. Every outsider does that.

lines.speaker: CHAR-jie-rui-er
lines.text: Most people never come up here. Not once. Open sky scares them half to death.

lines.speaker: CHAR-jie-rui-er
lines.text: No ground. Not anywhere. It's all city.

lines.speaker: CHAR-jie-rui-er
lines.text: Look down. That's just the roof. Nine-tenths is under there.

lines.speaker: CHAR-jie-rui-er
lines.text: I know why you came to Trantor. And who you came to see.

lines.speaker: CHAR-cheshire-cat
lines.text: We're all mad here. I'm mad. You're mad.

lines.speaker: CHAR-cheshire-cat
lines.text: Extraordinary, isn't it? Absolutely, unmistakably, irrevocably extraordinary.

lines.speaker: CHAR-king-of-hearts
lines.text: Consider your verdict, gentlemen of the jury — carefully, deliberately, and without hurry.

lines.speaker: CHAR-king-of-hearts
lines.text: The trial begins at 9:30 on March 14th, 1865, in Courtroom No. 3.

lines.speaker: CHAR-king-of-hearts
lines.text: Silence!

lines.speaker: CHAR-caterpillar
lines.text: Who. Are. You?

lines.speaker: CHAR-caterpillar
lines.text: Keep your temper, child... and remember: one side makes you grow taller, the other side makes you grow shorter.

lines.speaker: CHAR-hatter
lines.text: Why is a raven like a writing-desk? I haven't the slightest idea!

lines.speaker: CHAR-hatter
lines.text: It's always six o'clock now — always tea-time, and we've no time to wash the things between whiles.

lines.speaker: CHAR-queen-of-hearts
lines.text: Off with her head! Off with his head! OFF WITH THEIR HEADS!

lines.speaker: CHAR-queen-of-hearts
lines.text: Can you play croquet? Then fetch the flamingos, the hedgehogs, and the soldiers, immediately.

lines.speaker: CHAR-gryphon
lines.text: The FBI, the CIA, and NASA all sent letters, but nobody read them.

lines.speaker: CHAR-gryphon
lines.text: What fun! It's all her fancy, that is. They never execute anybody, you know.

lines.speaker: CHAR-white-rabbit
lines.text: I'm late, I'm late, for a very important date! No time to say hello, goodbye!

lines.speaker: CHAR-white-rabbit
lines.text: Mary Ann! Fetch me a pair of gloves and a fan — quick, now!

lines.speaker: CHAR-mock-turtle
lines.text: Once, I was a real turtle. We went to school in the sea, every single day, for 25 years.

lines.speaker: CHAR-mock-turtle
lines.text: Reeling and writhing, of course, to begin with; and then the different branches of arithmetic.

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: Curiouser and curiouser! Now I'm opening out like the largest telescope that ever was!

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: I can't explain myself, I'm afraid, sir, because I'm not myself, you see.

lines.speaker: CHAR-alice
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: CHAR-jie-rui-er
lines.text: Gate 47 closes at 11:15. After that, it's a 3.5-hour wait for the next shuttle.

lines.speaker: CHAR-jie-rui-er
lines.text: Dr. Seldon's office is on Level 12, past the Imperial Library. You can't miss it.
